Custom Product Page vs default listing

App Store Connect lets you publish up to 35 Custom Product Pages per app — each with its own URL for ads, influencer codes, email campaigns, and Product Page Optimization (PPO) tests. A CPP is not a mirror of your default product page. It can carry a different:

  • Subtitle — campaign-specific hook under the app name (~30 characters for zh-Hans)
  • Promotional text — time-limited news slot above the description (170 characters)
  • Description — long body tuned to the audience or offer behind the link
  • Screenshots and App Preview — alternate gallery frames with their own overlay caption lines

The default listing — name, default subtitle, default description, default screenshots, keywords, What's New, and IAP metadata — is what organic Search and browse traffic see. Localizing the default row in Connect does not localize your CPPs. Each CPP has its own localization matrix per locale.

This page covers one Custom Product Page rewritten for zh-Hans. For default listing fields, see our China storefront listing guide, subtitle guide, or description guide.

Why English-only CPPs waste China-targeted clicks

US and EU indie teams often ship CPPs in English first — sensible when testing creative in en-US Apple Search Ads or Meta campaigns. Problems start when the same English CPP URL backs a China storefront campaign:

  • Ad-to-landing mismatch — zh-Hans ad copy promises an outcome; the CPP subtitle and description are still English brochure text
  • Screenshot disconnect — Chinese overlay art on frame one, English captions on frames two through five
  • PPO false negatives — you conclude “China doesn’t convert on this angle” when the landing language never matched the traffic
  • Paid UA bleed — every click to an English CPP from a zh-Hans placement pays full CPI for a bounce you could fix in Connect

Apple falls back to the default listing locale when a CPP field is empty — but that default may not match your campaign angle. A China student-discount CPP needs Chinese copy about the offer, not your generic default description. Better CPP copy reduces landing-page bounce — it does not replace ad creative, bid strategy, or in-app UI localization.

What each CPP field does on zh-Hans

When you add a Simplified Chinese localization row to a specific Custom Product Page in App Store Connect, these fields are independent from the default listing’s zh-Hans row:

  • CPP subtitle — the hook under your app name on this page variant; can differ from default subtitle when the campaign targets a segment (e.g. “考研专注” vs generic “效率工具”)
  • CPP promotional text — 170-character slot for limited-time offers tied to the campaign (“开学季 7 天免费”)
  • CPP description — long body explaining the angle behind the deep link; can omit features irrelevant to this audience
  • CPP screenshot captions — short overlay lines on gallery frames assigned to this CPP; not the default gallery captions

App name and keyword field typically stay at the app level — this SKU does not rewrite default listing name, default keywords, What's New, IAP display names, or default screenshot sets. We focus on the CPP-specific copy slots above.

Common CPP localization mistakes

  • Assuming zh-Hans default listing copy auto-applies to every Custom Product Page
  • Pasting the default zh-Hans description into a segment-specific CPP — losing the campaign angle that justified a separate page
  • Localizing CPP screenshots in design tools but leaving English caption strings in Connect
  • Machine-translating the en-US CPP word-for-word — formal Chinese that reads nothing like your English product voice
  • Running PPO on zh-Hans traffic against an English CPP control — attributing poor results to audience fit instead of language fit
  • Forgetting promotional text on time-boxed China campaigns — empty slot when the offer is the whole point of the deep link

Each CPP exists because the default page is wrong for a segment or channel. zh-Hans CPP copy should preserve that intent in native Simplified Chinese — not collapse back to generic listing prose.

Paid UA, PPO, and when to localize CPPs first

Prioritize CPP localization when:

  • Apple Search Ads or third-party networks deep-link to a CPP URL on the China storefront
  • Product Page Optimization tests alternate subtitles or screenshots on zh-Hans traffic
  • Influencer or affiliate codes route to a campaign-specific page with English-only copy today
  • You A/B test creative angles per segment — student, pro, family — and each CPP has distinct English messaging

If organic Search is your only China channel and you never link to CPPs, start with the default listing instead. If ads or PPO already point at CPP URLs, fix the landing before you increase spend.
